SDV is both a generator and the referee: `src/data/generate_synethetic_datasets/SDV/` holds the generation scripts, and the evaluation notebooks for the SDV, MostlyAI and REaLTabFormer runs all import `sdv.evaluation.evaluate`, `sdv.utils.display_tables` and SDMetrics' multi-table `QualityReport`, with `sdv==0.18.0` and `sdmetrics==0.9.2` pinned. SDV's relational models and SDMetrics' multi-table report are run across every method in the comparison.

repo-trgan.summary: The reference implementation of TRGAN, a time-dependent GAN for synthetic transactional data from ITMO University. SDV appears in all three roles at once: `TRGAN_main.py` builds its own encoder from RDT's `ClusterBasedNormalizer`, `GaussianNormalizer` and `FrequencyEncoder`; `methods_comparison.py` fits `CopulaGANSynthesizer`, `CTGANSynthesizer` and `TVAESynthesizer` as the compared methods; and `evaluation_metrics.py` scores everything with SDMetrics' `TVComplement`, `NewRowSynthesis` and `ContingencySimilarity` over a `SingleTableMetadata`. RDT is inside the model, SDV's synthesizers are the baselines and SDMetrics is the scorecard.

repo-ai-ml-projects.summary: A personal collection of AI/ML coursework notebooks, including a retail sales-prediction project. The sales notebook contains commented-out code intended to generate synthetic sales data with CTGAN but explicitly notes it was never used, so the CTGAN synthesizer is only mentioned, not run.

repo-asid.summary: An AutoML tool from ITMO University for small and imbalanced tabular datasets, which selects a generative model to enlarge the sample before fitting a classifier. The model zoo it searches over is SDV's: `generative_model_estimation.py` imports `GaussianCopula`, `CTGAN`, `CopulaGAN` and `TVAE` from `sdv.tabular` and scores each candidate with `sdv.evaluation.evaluate`, with `sdv==0.17.1` pinned. SDV supplies both the candidates and the selection criterion.

repo-unece-synthetic-data-challenge.summary: Team D's entry to the UNECE High-Level Group for the Modernisation of Official Statistics synthetic data challenge, worked entirely in R Markdown across the SAT and ACS datasets. CTGAN is reached from R through reticulate: `6. GAN_SAT.Rmd` and `6. GAN_ACS_full.Rmd` set up a Python virtualenv, run `from ctgan import CTGANSynthesizer`, fit on the R data frame with the discrete columns named, and sample back into R, while the copula variants import `sdv.tabular.CopulaGAN` the same way. SDV's models are run inside an official-statistics evaluation, from R.

repo-bitcoin-fraud-prediction.summary: A machine-learning course project on the Elliptic Bitcoin dataset, trying to improve on the published results for classifying illicit transactions. One of its approaches is a whole script named for the model: `ctgan.py` imports `ctgan` and fits `ctgan.CTGANSynthesizer` to expand the heavily imbalanced illicit class. CTGAN is called as one of the project's rebalancing techniques.

repo-hanoi-artifact.summary: The PLDI 2020 artifact for Hanoi, an OCaml tool that infers representation invariants for data structures. The pooled match is the same name collision as the author's DSInvariant repository: `code/app/HanoiCmdLine.ml` instantiates the pipeline with a `ParSynthesizer` module of its own, whose name contains `PARSynthesizer` as a substring. OCaml only, no Python and no SDV-family dependency.

repo-scottishtaxbenefitmodel.summary: A microsimulation model of the Scottish fiscal system, computing the effect of tax and benefit changes on household incomes. SDV generates the shareable test population: a synthesis script imports `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer`, `CTGANSynthesizer`, `TVAESynthesizer` and the multi-table `HMASynthesizer` with `Metadata`, so household relational structure survives into a distributable mini-dataset. Fiscal policy modelling on confidential survey data made publishable through SDV.

repo-frootai.summary: A vendor-neutral catalogue of composable 'solution plays' for AI agents, each play carrying its own deployable skill files. Two plays package SDV as the synthesis step an agent executes: the synthetic-data-factory skill embeds `CTGANSynthesizer` with `SingleTableMetadata`, and the AI-data-marketplace skill embeds `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer`, both as runnable Python inside the `SKILL.md` an agent loads. SDV's single-table synthesizers ship as an invocable capability, with no dependency declared by the host repository.

SDV enters as subject matter: the analysis of arXiv 2506.17847, a comparative study of SDV against synthcity, decomposes `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer`, `CTGANSynthesizer` and `TVAESynthesizer` into their pipelines. Nothing is run; the corpus describes SDV's architecture at second hand.

It demonstrates that the generated synthetic anatomies show clinical realism and capture sub-population-specific anatomical variation across male and female cohorts. The work cites the CTGAN paper, but the available evidence does not show whether CTGAN itself is run as part of the AI component or merely referenced as related synthetic-data-generation work.

paper-detecting-intrusions-internet-ener.summary: This paper proposes an AutoML-based intrusion detection framework for Internet-of-Energy systems, focusing on battery energy storage systems, combining tree-based feature selection, Bayesian optimization, and stacking ensembles to improve detection accuracy and reduce training/inference time. The framework uses the TVAE algorithm for data balancing to address class imbalance in the intrusion-detection dataset. TVAE, the variational-autoencoder synthesizer described in the CTGAN paper, is run as the data-balancing component of the pipeline rather than being extended or benchmarked against.

paper-enhancing-intrusion-detection-imag.summary: This conference paper proposes a network intrusion detection framework that converts the NSL-KDD tabular dataset into image representations and trains a CNN for 5-class classification, using synthetic oversampling to counter severe class imbalance. Synthetic minority-class samples are generated with CTGAN before conversion to images and combined with RandomUnderSampler, yielding reported gains of up to 12.4% in F1-score over baselines. The paper cites the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper for the algorithm but explicitly generates the synthetic data using the third-party 'ydata-synthetic' Python library's CTGAN implementation rather than the SDV-family package.

paper-explainable-risk-calibrated-crop-2.summary: This paper proposes a crop recommendation framework that compares several ML classifiers (Gaussian Naive Bayes, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost), adds uncertainty calibration and SHAP-based explainability, and deploys the best model in a mobile app. To test robustness on unseen scenarios, the authors generate 500 synthetic samples from the crop dataset and evaluate all classifiers on this synthetic set. The synthetic data was produced using the SDV library's CTGAN implementation, run as a secondary generator to stress-test model generalizability.

paper-fed-dittab-diffusion-transformer-2.summary: This paper proposes Fed-DiTTab, a diffusion-transformer-based model for generating synthetic tabular data in a federated learning setting, where multiple clients collaboratively train a generative model without sharing raw data. The metadata gives no detail on how CTGAN is used, whether cited as prior art or run as a baseline. CTGAN is cited as a related tabular data generation method.

paper-generate-individual-spatiotemporal.summary: This article proposes a deep-learning approach to generate individual spatiotemporal activity sequences from synthesized population data, likely for use in transportation or urban simulation. Only metadata is available, so the specific methodology and experimental setup cannot be confirmed. The paper cites the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, indicating some engagement with SDV's CTGAN model, though how it is used could not be verified from the available evidence.

paper-ctab-gan-shap-constrained-2026.summary: This paper proposes MS-CTAB-GAN+, a conditional tabular GAN for heart disease data augmentation under small-sample, high-missingness conditions, built on the CTAB-GAN+ framework and augmented with a miceforest-based imputation stage and a SHAP-Constraint Module that injects real-data feature-importance patterns into the generator's training objective. Experiments on the UCI Heart Disease dataset show downstream classifiers trained on MS-CTAB-GAN+ synthetic data outperform those trained on data from CTAB-GAN, CTAB-GAN+, and CTGAN. CTGAN is cited as the origin of mode-specific normalization for conditional tabular data generation and is also run as one of several baseline generators compared against the proposed method in the experiments.

paper-measuring-privacy-risks-tradeoffs-.summary: This paper is an empirical study of the privacy-utility tradeoff for tabular financial synthetic data generators, comparing Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, TVAE, and TabDiff on quality, downstream utility, and privacy metrics (including membership inference attacks and distance-to-closest-record scores) across balanced and imbalanced financial datasets. Its central technical contribution is a new differentially private reimplementation of CTGAN and TVAE (DP-CTGAN, DP-TVAE) that redesigns the conditional-vector sampling and per-sample gradient-penalty accounting to close unaccounted privacy leaks. SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer is run as an evaluation baseline and CTGAN/TVAE (and their mode-specific normalization and conditional vector mechanism) are directly modified into new DP variants that form the paper's core contribution.

paper-predicting-pulmonary-function-deep.summary: This clinical study develops predictive models for pulmonary function tests (FVC and FEV1) in patients unable to undergo standard testing before emergency surgery, using data from 930 patients across two hospitals. The authors compare traditional linear models (MLR, GLM) against neural network models trained on an expanded dataset of 100,000 synthetic records, finding the neural network approach more accurate for FVC and FEV1 in males. CTGAN is the generator used to produce the large synthetic training set that underlies the whole neural-network modeling exercise.

paper-prism-private-relational-synthesis.summary: This paper presents Prism, an end-to-end framework for differentially private (DP) relational data synthesis that distills knowledge from an ensemble of teacher LLMs into a student generator via DP output aggregation, using token pruning, adaptive noise scaling, and threshold-filtered probabilistic sampling to improve the privacy-utility trade-off. It is evaluated against eight state-of-the-art baselines across twelve experiments on tabular datasets like Adult. CTGAN is cited as the base architecture underlying two DP baseline methods, DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN, which are run as comparison baselines but not CTGAN itself.

paper-machine-learning-model-simulation-.summary: This conference paper proposes an MCS-Ensemble framework for Type 2 diabetes risk prediction, combining XGBoost, Random Forest, Multilayer Perceptron and SVM in a stacked ensemble, with Monte Carlo simulation used to quantify prediction uncertainty and imbalance-handling and feature-selection techniques applied to improve performance. Evaluation is performed on the PIMA Indian Diabetes Dataset and a harmonised NHS-derived clinical subset. CTGAN appears in a comparison table of class-imbalance handling techniques, described by its conditional design and known mode-collapse limitation for rare subgroups, without clear evidence it was actually executed as part of the study's own pipeline.

paper-synthetic-augmentation-structured-.summary: This paper proposes a data-centric framework for visual geo-localization that encodes images into interpretable 'Structured Templates' capturing environmental, infrastructural, and cultural attributes via a vision-language model, then augments underrepresented countries in a long-tail YFCC100M subset using tabular oversampling methods. It compares SMOTENC, ADASYN, KMeans-SMOTE, and CTGAN as synthetic sampling techniques applied to the encoded template feature vectors, finding SMOTENC best overall but CTGAN competitive for countries with complex geographic patterns. CTGAN is run as one of several oversampling baselines on structured tabular feature representations, not as the paper's proposed method.

paper-synthetic-energy-generation-wasser.summary: This article tackles synthetic tabular data generation for energy-consumption modeling of high-performance computing nodes, proposing a Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty to create realistic synthetic data when real measurements are scarce and costly to obtain. The generated data are validated via statistical similarity to real data and shown to improve energy estimation models, outperforming a regression-oriented baseline (SMONG). The authors' approach combined ideas from Tabular GAN (TGAN) with the Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty architecture, using TGAN as a design component folded into their own generative model.

paper-team-then-trim-assembly-2026.summary: This paper proposes Team-then-Trim (T2), a framework that generates synthetic tabular data via a collaborative team of LLMs each producing different data components sequentially, followed by a three-stage quality-control pipeline, aiming to address class imbalance, selection bias, and low fidelity in small tabular datasets. It is evaluated against several baselines on simulated and real-world datasets (COMPAS, drug, diabetes, travel behavior) using downstream utility and data-quality metrics. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of several deep generative baselines compared against T2, consistently underperforming it.

paper-ctrtab-high-dimensional-limited-sa.summary: Observes that diffusion-based tabular synthesizers degrade as column count grows, to the point of losing to simpler non-diffusion models, and attributes this to limited training samples in high-dimensional space; proposes CtrTab, which injects data-aware noise into a latent diffusion model as a regularizer and shows analytically that the added noise term acts as a penalty on the gradient of the score network. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the six baselines run against it, alongside SMOTE, TabDDPM, RelDDPM and TabSyn, with competitor hyperparameters taken from the TabSyn paper, and the related-work section credits CTGAN with incorporating class labels in the generator to produce data conditioned on the target class and notes that CTAB-GAN+ extends CTGAN to continuous class labels. CTGAN and TVAE are therefore executed as comparison baselines whose degradation at high dimensionality motivates the proposed model, with nothing of CTGAN carried into CtrTab's architecture.

paper-driven-digital-twin-student-2025.summary: This paper proposes a data-driven digital twin approach that models student engagement on Learning Management Systems while preserving missingness patterns, rather than removing or imputing missing values as prior work does. Using reversible data transformations, the authors train CTGAN, TVAE, and RealTabFormer to generate synthetic virtual replicas of students' learning activity data, then train XGBoost on the balanced synthetic data to predict engagement levels (F1 above 80%). CTGAN and TVAE are run through the Synthetic Data Vault's SDV Python package (with RDT for the reversible transformations and SDMetrics for quality reporting and conditional sampling used to generate balanced samples), making SDV's tabular synthesizers and evaluation tooling the core generative and evaluation engine for the whole empirical study.

paper-text-tabular-generate-synthetic-20.summary: This paper proposes a text-to-tabular method that uses large language models to generate synthetic patient data from a textual database description alone, without access to original patient-level data, targeting privacy-limited healthcare research settings. The authors evaluate their zero-shot LLM approach against state-of-the-art synthetic data generation models on fidelity, privacy, and utility metrics for two clinical datasets (PPMI and ADNI). CTGAN, TVAE, and a Gaussian Copula model are run unmodified as comparison baselines, and evaluation relies on SDMetrics' fidelity metrics (e.g. Column Shapes, Column Pair Trends), making SDV's synthesizers and SDMetrics quality-report tooling the empirical backbone against which the proposed LLM generator is measured.

paper-access-control-policy-generation-2.summary: This conference paper proposes generating access control policy data for IoT systems using deep generative models, evaluated via a case study on the CAV policies dataset from Cunnington et al. The authors train CTGAN and CopulaGAN both with and without environmental constraints, then assess results using synthesis (quality) scores, visual correlation comparisons, and TSTR-style ML efficacy F1 tests across multiple classifiers. SDV's CTGAN and CopulaGAN are run as the two baseline generative models producing all the synthetic access-control policy data the empirical study rests on.

The abstract and available evidence give no detail on how the dataset was generated or expanded. The paper cites the TGAN (2018) paper from the SDV family, but the evidence does not show it being run or engaged with.

paper-evolution-generative-adversarial-n.summary: A PRISMA-guided systematic review of 81 peer-reviewed studies on GAN-based synthetic data generation across medical imaging, EHRs, genomics, and multimodal healthcare datasets, mapping architectures, evaluation strategies, and ethical/regulatory barriers to clinical adoption. The review does not run any generative models itself but synthesizes and tabulates findings from prior work, describing CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN as prominent tabular architectures noted in the literature for handling mixed data types, class imbalance, and privacy-preserving EHR synthesis. CTGAN's conditional generation and mode-specific normalization, along with TVAE and CopulaGAN, are discussed in prose as methods reported by surveyed papers rather than executed by the authors.

paper-explainable-machine-learning-model.summary: This retrospective clinical study built an explainable machine-learning model predicting 1-year readmission risk in patients with acute exacerbations of COPD, combining missing-data imputation, relief-based feature selection, and tree-based classifiers (XGBoost, LightGBM, random forest) interpreted via SHAP. To counter limited sample size and overfitting, CTGAN was applied to the derivation cohort to generate synthetic augmented samples (150% of original size) before model training. CTGAN's conditional tabular GAN, run as a Python library alongside scikit-learn and XGBoost, was the generator producing the synthetic data that underpinned the reported gains in model generalisation.

paper-gans-fine-tuning-transfer-2025.summary: This paper studies synthetic electronic health record generation for Chronic Kidney Disease using medGAN and CorGAN architectures augmented with WGAN and WGAN-GP loss functions, and investigates transfer learning to fine-tune these models between a larger and a smaller CKD dataset. Random Forest classifiers trained on real, synthetic, and mixed data are evaluated to show that transfer-learning-generated synthetic data improves classifier performance, with F1-scores improving by up to 74.3%. CTGAN is discussed only in related work as a prior tabular-GAN approach that introduces an alternative data normalization method and a conditional generator, but it is not implemented or run in the experiments.

paper-synthetic-flow-nids-2025.summary: Builds one evaluation pipeline for synthetic network-flow data and puts a representative of each generative family through it — a GAN, a diffusion model and a language model — measuring not only distributional similarity but the downstream intrusion-detection performance that follows from training on the generated flows, with attention to minority attack classes. CTGAN is the GAN-family representative: it gets its own methodology subsection describing the conditional generator and training strategy that address mode collapse and imbalanced categoricals, its training and sampling workflow is diagrammed, and it is trained and sampled on the benchmark flows.

paper-overcoming-scarcity-edge-federated.summary: This paper proposes a federated learning framework for distributed solar power forecasting that addresses data scarcity at edge clients by augmenting local training data with GAN-generated synthetic time-series samples during initialization. An LSTM forecaster is trained under FedAvg aggregation across nine simulated clients, and the augmentation approach is compared against a no-augmentation baseline and SMOTE-based augmentation. CopulaGAN, SDV's tabular generative model, is used throughout as the actual synthetic-data generator whose output drives the empirical results, seeded with global weights and fine-tuned locally at each client.

paper-palsyn-dp-event-log-2025.summary: Generates synthetic process-mining event logs that carry control-flow, timing and data attributes together under a formal differential-privacy guarantee, using a private autoregressive sequence model with DP-K-Means discretization of numerical attributes and composition theorems to account the privacy budget, and compares trace-level fidelity against PRIPEL. CTGAN is the tabular precedent the discretization is reasoned against rather than a model that is run: the authors state their numerical handling adapts Xu et al.'s method, substituting DP-K-Means for the Gaussian mixture that CTGAN uses.

paper-subpopulation-specific-synthetic-e.summary: This paper proposes a GAN-based ensemble framework that generates subpopulation-specific synthetic EHR data to improve mortality-prediction fairness and performance for underrepresented patient groups in MIMIC-derived datasets. The authors train a separate CTGAN per underperforming subpopulation to augment its training data before fitting XGBoost/gradient-boosting classifiers, comparing against SMOTE and no-augmentation baselines. CTGAN is run as the core synthetic-data generator underpinning the entire empirical evaluation, with hyperparameters (discriminator/generator learning rates, discriminator steps, epochs, batch size) matching the CTGAN constructor's own parameters.

paper-synthetic-nutritional-generation-v.summary: This conference paper proposes NutriSynth, a differential-privacy-enabled variational autoencoder framework with attention-based interpretability and adversarial debiasing for generating synthetic nutritional profiles of vulnerable populations (children, elderly, food-insecure households). It reports gains in fidelity, fairness, and privacy over several baseline synthetic-data methods on 8,000 nutritional profiles. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of six baseline generators in comparative tables of data utility, privacy attack resistance, and fairness metrics, against which the authors' own NutriSynth is shown to outperform.

paper-treecsp-efficient-way-generate-202.summary: This paper introduces TreeCSP, a Tree-based Chained Sampling Pools framework for population synthesis in agent-based transport models, which organizes household and person generation via a hierarchical relationship tree and multi-step sampling to better capture complex household structures than existing methods. The authors benchmark two TreeCSP variants (CSP-Seed and CSP-BN) against IPU and CTGAN using the VISTA travel survey dataset, measuring Jensen-Shannon Distance across household and relationship attributes. CTGAN, explicitly implemented based on the original CTGAN paper, is run as one of the baseline generators for synthesizing individual-level data and is consistently outperformed by the proposed methods.

paper-2llm-multi-view-molecular-2024.summary: This paper designs a novel GAN for augmenting small, high-dimensional survey data (258 persons who use drugs) with built-in skip-logic constraint handling, used to improve classifiers predicting short-term changes in substance use. The proposed model directly extends CTGAN's conditional generator, training-by-sampling procedure, and mode-specific normalization, adding an auxiliary classifier and downstream/skip-logic losses, and is benchmarked against CTGAN, TVAE, TableGAN, CTABGAN+, and TabDDPM. CTGAN's conditional vector and mode-specific normalization are the architectural foundation the authors build their new generator on top of.

paper-model-informed-clinical-trial-2024.summary: This tutorial describes how to build an R Shiny-based graphical interface for model-informed clinical trial simulation, illustrated with a tool developed for Duchenne muscular dystrophy that generates a virtual population to enlarge simulated sample sizes, validated against a real placebo-arm trial. The authors compared machine learning approaches for generating this virtual population, including CTGAN and synthpop, finding synthpop performed better and was more stable in resembling the real covariate distributions and correlations for their case example. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of two candidate generators for the virtual population and rejected in favor of synthpop.

paper-transfer-learning-cnn-dynamic-2024.summary: This paper proposes a dynamic security assessment (DSA) model for power systems that combines CTGAN-based data augmentation with a CNN classifier and transfer-learning fine-tuning to handle small datasets and unknown fault/topology conditions, tested on the IEEE 39-bus system. CTGAN is used to expand an original 1,150-point database to 10,350 points, with its synthetic data quality evaluated via Wasserstein Distance and FID against a plain GAN. The paper's hyperparameter table (generator/discriminator dimension, weight decay, learning rate, batch size) matches CTGAN's own constructor parameters, indicating the sdv-dev package was run. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator/training-by-sampling techniques are the load-bearing data-augmentation mechanism underlying the whole empirical study.

paper-algorithm-generation-adg-engine-20.summary: This paper presents the ADG Engine, a system that generates synthetic user behavioral datasets—covering both normal and abnormal activity—without requiring initial seed data, aimed at supporting data analytics in domains where real data are scarce, sensitive, or unavailable. It allows users to customize the ratio of normal to abnormal behavior to support anomaly-related analytics tasks. The paper cites Patki et al.'s Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) as prior work on generating synthetic data for relational databases, without running or extending it.

paper-green-building-cost-ctgan-2024.summary: Estimates construction costs at the early project stage, where owners of green building projects have too few comparable past projects to reason from and cannot separate green-specific costs from baseline ones. CTGAN generates the missing comparables, and the title makes SDV's synthesizer the named basis of the method.

paper-conditional-gan-intrusion-detectio.summary: Pairs a generative adversarial network with a deep residual network for intrusion detection on NSL-KDD, converting every record to a greyscale image so ResNet-18 can read it, and reports good generalisation to unseen attack types. CTGAN supplies extra training samples for those unknown attacks — one component of the pipeline, named as a method with no library attached, so the mechanism is unconfirmed.
paper-conditional-gan-intrusion-detectio.needs: IEEE Xplore is paywalled to automated fetches; confirm the CTGAN implementation.

paper-federated-analytics-dg-2024.summary: Augments training data across federated clients to improve domain generalization in network analytics, using DCGAN for the generation itself. CTGAN appears in the bibliography but nowhere in the method, so the link is a reference rather than a use.

paper-uav-jamming-gan-2024.summary: Manufactures jamming attack data for unmanned aerial vehicles, since real attack traces are scarce and intrusion detection cannot be trained without them. CTGAN and Gaussian copulas generate those traces; the same authors' later IEEE Access paper extends this to spoofing.

paper-handling-imbalanced-beyond-network.summary: This paper develops and compares four generative models (CTGAN, CopulaGAN, GaussianCopula, TVAE) to generate synthetic tabular data addressing class imbalance in a 5G/beyond network management dataset, evaluating them via quality and diagnostic reports. The whole synthetic-data generation and evaluation pipeline is implemented directly with the SDV Python library (v1.5.0) and its SDMetrics module, running SDV's own CTGAN, CopulaGAN, GaussianCopula and TVAE synthesizers as the models under comparison.

paper-thermal-comfort-ctgan-2024.summary: Thermal comfort models are limited by small occupant-survey datasets, so this combines feature selection with generated data to enlarge the training set. CTGAN is trained on the survey data and the models fitted to its output are the ones reported.

paper-intrusion-detection-scp-ctgan-2024.summary: This paper proposes two compressed deep learning models—LIDSuFNN and LIDSuCNN—for intrusion detection on resource-constrained IoT devices, using neuron/filter pruning and quantization to reduce training time and memory while maintaining accuracy comparable to baselines. To supplement training and testing, the authors generate synthetic intrusion detection data. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run to produce this synthetic data used across the experimental pipeline.
paper-intrusion-detection-scp-ctgan-2024.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev package or reimplemented, nor whether the conditional vector was specifically leveraged for class balance.

paper-leveraging-human-loop-machine-2024.summary: This conference paper proposes an intrusion detection system for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks that combines Human-in-the-Loop Machine Learning with GAN-synthesized data to overcome the scarcity of labeled UAV intrusion datasets, training and evaluating detectors on a mix of real (CIC-IDS2017) and synthetic traffic. CTGAN is used as the synthetic data generator, described with its conditional generator formulation for handling discrete and continuous tabular fields, and its output quality is checked via distributional similarity scores before being fed into the intrusion-detection pipeline. CTGAN's conditional generation and mode-specific handling of mixed data types form the load-bearing data-generation stage of the paper's empirical pipeline.
paper-leveraging-human-loop-machine-2024.needs: Unclear whether the authors ran the sdv-dev CTGAN package or reimplemented the conditional generator themselves from the paper's equations; no import, package name, or hyperparameter table is given to confirm library use versus reimplementation.

paper-managing-secondary-risks-optimal-2.summary: This paper, published in a risk/reliability engineering context, proposes an optimal risk response strategy paired with resource scheduling for managing secondary risks arising from risk mitigation actions. It cites the CTGAN paper from the SDV family, but no citing sentence or full text is available to establish how or whether CTGAN was actually used.
paper-managing-secondary-risks-optimal-2.needs: Full text and citing sentence not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was run, adopted in method, or merely cited in passing among references.

paper-optimizing-rare-disease-gait-2024.summary: This study evaluates whether generative AI can compensate for the small, imbalanced datasets typical of rare-disease gait research, using inertial sensor data from 30 people with hereditary cerebellar ataxia and 100 healthy controls. The authors compare subsampling, oversampling, SMOTE, a standard GAN, and a conditional tabular GAN (ctGAN) for generating synthetic minority-class data fed into a random forest classifier, finding ctGAN gave the best balance of classification accuracy and explainability while preserving statistical consistency with real gait features. CTGAN is run as the primary data-balancing generator, evaluated against several other augmentation methods and shown to yield the strongest improvement in downstream classification performance.
paper-optimizing-rare-disease-gait-2024.needs: No explicit statement of which CTGAN implementation/library was used (e.g., sdv-dev's ctgan package vs. custom code); classified as api_user based on standard terminology and lack of described custom architecture, but this is not fully certain.

paper-defect-augmentation-display-manufa.summary: This conference paper proposes a defect-data augmentation pipeline for display manufacturing, combining over/under-sampling, anomaly scoring, and kernel/XAI-based feature selection to address the extreme class imbalance between defective and normal samples that hampers machine learning model performance. The authors report that standard GAN/VAE approaches perform poorly on tabular/numeric process data compared to image data, so they apply CT-GAN specifically to increase the number of defect samples and show improved augmentation performance. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as the core generator for synthesizing minority-class defect data.
paper-defect-augmentation-display-manufa.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract/metadata available, so exact integration (library use vs reimplementation) and venue name could not be confirmed.

paper-cross-table-masked-pretraining-202.summary: This paper proposes CM2, a cross-table pretraining framework for tabular data that combines a semantic-aware tabular neural network with a novel pretraining objective (prompt Masked Table Modeling), aiming to generalize across heterogeneous tables the way NLP pretraining generalizes across text corpora. It contributes a large real-world multi-table dataset and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on downstream tabular prediction tasks. CTGAN is only cited in the reference list as prior tabular-data-modeling work, with no evidence it was run in the study.
paper-cross-table-masked-pretraining-202.needs: Confirmed bibliographic-only citation; no engagement with CTGAN in the body.

paper-adversary-model-fraudsters-behavio.summary: This paper proposes ADVO, a time-dependent oversampling strategy for credit card fraud detection that models the temporal relationship among frauds, implemented via a regression-based predictor and an adapted TimeGAN approach, and evaluates it against several oversampling baselines on real and simulated transaction data. CTGAN is included as one of the comparison oversampling methods, run with its default two-layer generator/discriminator architecture, and its mode-specific normalization and conditional generator design are described in related work. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is used here as one of several baseline oversamplers benchmarked against the authors' proposed ADV-O method.

paper-level-hybrid-strategy-selection-20.summary: This paper addresses severe class imbalance in hard-disk SMART data by training three tabular generative models -- CTGAN, CopulaGAN and CTAB-GAN -- to synthesize minority (failure) samples, then mixing their outputs and using a genetic algorithm to select the best combination for training disk-failure classifiers. Results tables report classification metrics for each generator individually and for the hybrid mixture across several classifiers (ANN, SVM, Decision Tree, Bayes, RandomForest). CTGAN and CopulaGAN, both part of SDV's synthesizer suite, are run directly with explicit hyperparameters (e.g. epochs=300) as two of the three generative models whose synthetic minority-class data drive the whole empirical evaluation.
paper-level-hybrid-strategy-selection-20.needs: CTGAN is mis-cited as 'proposed by Xu L at NeurIPS 2020' (actual venue/year is NeurIPS 2019); recorded as the paper states it.

paper-findiff-diffusion-models-financial.summary: FinDiff is a diffusion model that generates mixed-type financial tabular data (categorical and numeric) for regulatory downstream tasks like stress testing and fraud detection, using embedding encodings to unify modalities. It is benchmarked against TVAE, CTGAN, and TabDDPM on three financial datasets (credit default, municipal payments, and fund holdings) using fidelity, utility, synthesis, and privacy metrics. The SDV library (v1.0.1) supplied the TVAE and CTGAN baseline implementations and the evaluation metrics used throughout the comparison.

paper-gdts-gan-distributed-tabular-2023.summary: This paper proposes GDTS, a distributed framework for training GAN-based tabular synthesizers across decentralized data sources under federated-learning (FL) and multi-discriminator (MD) paradigms, introducing a privacy-preserving multi-source feature encoding and a table-similarity weighting strategy to handle non-IID clients. The empirical evaluation trains a CTGAN model distributed across clients, adapting CTGAN's default column encoding (VGM for continuous, one-hot for categorical) into the new distributed architecture and comparing GDTS_FL against GDTS_MD variants. CTGAN's mode-specific feature encoding and training procedure are extended into a novel distributed architecture, making CTGAN the load-bearing generator whose encoding scheme the whole distributed framework is built around.
paper-gdts-gan-distributed-tabular-2023.needs: Unclear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package itself was invoked or whether the authors reimplemented CTGAN's encoding/training within their own distributed framework; treated as derivative_work given the architectural modification for distributed training.

paper-ship-engine-health-monitoring-2023.summary: Preliminary study on monitoring a ship's engine with ordinary classifiers — logistic regression, KNN, naive Bayes, SVC, decision tree — where no real fault data is at hand, so the study runs on simulated data instead. The paper is explicit that the data was made with SDV and that several of the library's models were compared before the classifiers were fitted, which makes it the source of everything downstream.
paper-ship-engine-health-monitoring-2023.needs: IEEE Xplore is paywalled to automated fetches; confirm which SDV models were compared and on what basis one was chosen.

paper-individual-level-functional-connec.summary: This neuroimaging study uses support vector regression models built on individually-estimated functional connectivity between frontoparietal, dorsal attention, cingulo-opercular, and default-mode networks to predict cognitive-control behaviors (switching and inhibiting) from two in-scanner tasks. The authors report that inter-network connectivity, particularly involving the lateral default-mode network, predicts these behaviors across individuals. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular generative adversarial network, is cited as the method used to generate synthetic data for the study, though the surrounding methodological detail is not present in the available evidence.
paper-individual-level-functional-connec.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear what role the synthetic data played in the study's analysis pipeline (e.g., data augmentation, validation, or privacy) or how central CTGAN was to the overall empirical programme.

paper-multi-stage-classification-scheme-.summary: This paper proposes a feedforward-neural-network-driven, multi-stage ensemble architecture that sequentially predicts drugs, features, and final discharge location for ICU patients across recovery stages. Because some stage-specific datasets (e.g., diabetic ketoacidosis) contain only 16 observations, the author augments them to 5000 observations before model fitting. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) package is run directly, using its TVAE synthesizer as the data-augmentation generator underlying this small-data medical pipeline.

paper-quality-synthetic-generated-tabula.summary: This paper surveys and categorizes utility measures for evaluating the quality of synthetic tabular data used to augment minority classes under class imbalance, applying them across two datasets (Adults Income, Liar+) and five generative methods. It compares Borderline SMOTE, DataSynthesizer, CTGAN, CopulaGAN, and REaLTabFormer using univariate, bivariate, multivariate, and classification-based utility measures. CTGAN and the 'synthetic data vault CopulaGAN model' are run as two of the five generators whose synthetic output is evaluated and compared throughout the study.

paper-reinforcement-bond-performance-con.summary: This work presents an explainable ensemble machine-learning model to predict reinforcement bond performance in 3D concrete printing, using deep generative adversarial network methods to augment a limited experimental dataset. The paper cites the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, but the evidence available (title and metadata only) does not confirm whether the SDV-family CTGAN implementation was actually run or only cited as prior GAN-based tabular synthesis work. CTGAN is referenced in connection with the paper's generative data-augmentation approach.
paper-reinforcement-bond-performance-con.needs: Full text or citing sentence needed to determine whether CTGAN (SDV package) was actually run for data augmentation, reimplemented independently, or merely cited among GAN literature.

paper-atualiza-modelo-baseado-aumento-20.summary: This paper proposes a scheme for updating machine-learning-based network intrusion detection models using GAN-based data augmentation followed by transfer learning, aiming to reduce the number of labeled instances and computational cost needed for periodic model updates. Experiments on an 8TB, one-year network traffic dataset show reduced false positive rates and lower update cost compared to full retraining. CTGAN is retrained at each model update cycle to generate augmented traffic instances (10% of the training set), serving as the sole data-augmentation generator underlying the proposal's empirical results.
paper-atualiza-modelo-baseado-aumento-20.needs: No package name, import, or constructor parameters are given for the CTGAN implementation, so it is unclear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run or a custom reimplementation was used.

paper-improving-medical-predictions-labe.summary: This paper proposes a semi-supervised learning approach for denoising machine-learning predictions on medical datasets, combining a small pool of correctly labelled instances with a large pool of noisy or unlabelled ones, evaluated on a diabetes diagnostic dataset. To create the large training pools needed for their experiments, the authors generate synthetic tabular examples using CTGAN and TVAE while preserving class-conditional densities and class imbalance ratios, then measure classifier performance and KL divergence on this synthetic data. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE algorithms are run directly as the synthetic data generators underpinning the paper's entire experimental evaluation.
paper-improving-medical-predictions-labe.needs: Not fully clear whether the sdv-dev CTGAN/SDV package was directly imported or the authors reimplemented the algorithms; no hyperparameter table or package name is given, so api_user vs port is inferred rather than confirmed.

paper-low-sample-classification-nids-202.summary: This paper adapts the semi-supervised EC-GAN framework to tabular network-flow data, replacing its original image-domain GAN with a Wasserstein Conditional GAN with Gradient Penalty (WCGAN-GP) to generate synthetic samples that help a DNN classifier trained on small, imbalanced slices of the CIC-IDS-2017 intrusion-detection dataset. The authors show their modified EC-GAN can match prior detection results using as little as 25% of the original data. CTGAN and TGAN (Xu et al. 2019; Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) are named as alternative tabular-data GAN solutions the authors considered before choosing WCGAN-GP, but neither is implemented or run.
paper-low-sample-classification-nids-202.needs: CTGAN/TGAN are only briefly discussed as considered alternatives, not run; confirms citation_only rather than baseline_only.

paper-permutation-invariant-synthesis-20.summary: Shows that state-of-the-art tabular synthesizers are sensitive to the order of the input columns, a dependence that should not exist for data with no intrinsic column ordering, and proposes a permutation-invariant treatment. CTGAN and TVAE are among the models whose sensitivity is demonstrated, so the criticism lands directly on SDV's synthesizers.

paper-security-alert-screening-2022.summary: Addresses the false alarms and missed detections that follow from skewed alert distributions in intrusion detection. CTGAN oversamples the specific alert classes that are under-observed, using its conditional sampling to target named categories rather than the minority class as a whole.

paper-use-generative-adversarial-network.summary: A survey of the past seven years of research applying GAN architectures to class-imbalanced tabular data, covering domains from network traffic classification to financial transactions and identifying which methodologies and experimental factors most improve machine learning efficacy. It reviews and summarizes prior published works rather than running its own experiments, describing methods such as CGAN variants, SMOTE-based baselines, and autoencoder alternatives. CTGAN and its predecessor TGAN are discussed in detail as prior work, including CTGAN's variational Gaussian mixture mode-specific preprocessing and its benchmarked comparison against TVAE and other architectures reported in the original CTGAN paper, but neither is run by the survey's own authors.
paper-use-generative-adversarial-network.needs: Survey discusses CTGAN/TGAN methodology and results from the original papers in detail (engagement beyond a passing mention) but the survey's own authors run no experiments with SDV code.

paper-topology-preserving-feature-correl.summary: This short theoretical paper investigates whether preserving the topological structure of synthetic tabular data—via persistent homology and homeomorphism between original and synthetic data spaces—can preserve pairwise feature correlations, which GAN-based synthesizers otherwise fail to retain. The authors import a CTGAN model from its GitHub repository, generate synthetic data for datasets including a wine-quality dataset, and empirically show that CT-GAN's output has dissimilar 0th and 1st homology groups from the real data, evidencing broken feature correlations. CTGAN (with its mode-specific normalization) is the sole generative model run in the study, serving as the empirical subject whose correlation-preservation failure motivates the paper's topological hypothesis.
paper-topology-preserving-feature-correl.needs: The paper cites CTGAN via the ctgan-neurips-2019 paper but also lists tgan-2018 in cites_which_sdv_papers per OpenAlex metadata; the body text and reference [8] clearly refer to CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019), not TGAN.

paper-ictgan-gait-2022.summary: Gait authentication systems can be defeated by random-vector attacks, and the defence proposed here is to widen the variance of the impostor samples the classifier trains against. iCTGAN is CTGAN applied to an impostor feature matrix, trained with Wasserstein loss to synthesise those samples.

paper-open-generator-synthetic-administr.summary: This conference paper presents an open-source generator designed to produce synthetic administrative healthcare databases, likely for research or software-testing purposes where real patient records cannot be shared. Little further detail on its methodology is available from the evidence provided. The work cites CTGAN, the SDV-family generative model for tabular data, apparently as part of its discussion of synthetic data generation approaches.
paper-open-generator-synthetic-administr.needs: Only metadata and a non-informative abstract ('International audience') were available; full text needed to determine whether CTGAN was run, adapted, or merely cited as related work.

paper-deep-generative-models-counter-202.summary: This paper studies which deep generative model (GAN, VAE, or RBM) best pairs with which classification metric for oversampling minority classes under different degrees of class imbalance, proposing an optimum-proportion methodology and comparing results against established data-synthesizing baselines. The GAN stream of their three-model comparison is implemented using the default CTGAN package. CTGAN is thus run as one of the three generative-model families whose oversampled data is evaluated against precision, recall, F1, AUC, G-Mean and balanced accuracy.
paper-deep-generative-models-counter-202.needs: Full text does not explicitly show library name 'sdv'/'ctgan' import; identification of ref [78] as CTGAN relies on OpenAlex citation mapping rather than a directly quoted package name in the passage.

paper-reply-rc3-2-2021.summary: This is an author reply to a reviewer comment (RC3) accompanying a study exploring whether copula-based statistical models can generate synthetic training data to improve machine-learning emulators of physical processes, tested on a toy model of downwelling longwave radiation. The associated paper reports up to 62% improvement in mean absolute error for a neural-network emulator trained with copula-augmented data. It cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) DSAA 2016 paper as prior work on copula-based synthetic data generation, without evidence in this excerpt that the SDV software itself was run.
paper-reply-rc3-2-2021.needs: Full text not obtained; this is a peer-review reply document rather than the main article, and it is unclear whether the authors ran SDV's software directly or only cite its copula concept as prior art.

paper-insurance-fraud-tgan-2021.summary: Separates fraud detection into a preprocessing phase and a classification phase and asks whether the choice made in the first constrains what the second can achieve. TGAN is the generative option set against SMOTE, MWMOTE and ADASYN, so the first-party tabular GAN is benchmarked against three classical oversamplers on insurance claims.

paper-addressing-spatial-sparsity-mdt-20.summary: This paper proposes a framework to combat spatial sparsity in Minimization of Drive Test (MDT) cellular network reports by augmenting sparse tabular data with generative models, evaluating synthetic data quality via statistical resemblance measures, downstream ML task performance, and comparison against classical ML baselines. The authors build their own GAN and VAE data augmentation models, explicitly stating they 'employ and modify' generative models 'from the synthesizer in [28]', i.e., the TGAN paper. TGAN's tabular GAN synthesizer design is adapted and reimplemented as the basis for the paper's own generative models rather than run as a library.
paper-addressing-spatial-sparsity-mdt-20.needs: Unclear exactly how much of the modified GAN architecture derives directly from TGAN's design versus original contribution, since no architectural details are given in the excerpted text.

paper-gan-training-gans-specific-2020.summary: This paper proposes AE-OT-GAN, a generative model that combines an autoencoder, a semi-discrete optimal transport map in the latent space, and a GAN to overcome mode collapse/mixture while producing sharp images, tested on MNIST, CIFAR10 and CelebA. It compares FID scores against several state-of-the-art GAN baselines including WGAN-GP, PGGAN, SNGAN, WGAN-div, WGAN-QC and 'CTGAN' on these image datasets. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is cited via the Xu et al. NeurIPS 2019 paper and listed as one of several comparison baselines, though its use here for image (not tabular) generation is unusual and possibly a mis-citation of the model name.
paper-gan-training-gans-specific-2020.needs: CTGAN is a tabular-data model but is here compared via FID on image datasets (CIFAR10, CelebA); unclear whether the authors actually ran SDV's CTGAN code adapted to images or mis-cited a different image-GAN under the same acronym.

paper-predicting-ultra-high-performance-.summary: This paper develops machine learning models (random forest, extra trees, gradient boosting) to predict the compressive strength of ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC), addressing the scarcity of experimental data by generating thousands of synthetic training samples. Tabular generative adversarial networks (TGAN) were used to generate 6513 synthetic UHPC mixture-property data points, which trained the regression models later tested on 810 real experimental observations. SDV's TGAN model is the generator whose synthetic output the entire empirical training programme rests on.
paper-predicting-ultra-high-performance-.needs: Full text describing the actual generation pipeline (library import or hyperparameters) was not shown; inferred TGAN was run as an actual tool from the method description rather than seeing code/library references directly.

paper-synthea-coronavirus-covid-model-20.summary: This paper describes the construction of a COVID-19 disease progression and treatment model for the open-source Synthea patient simulation, which generated 124,150 synthetic patients with calibrated symptoms, hospitalization, and mortality outcomes based on early-pandemic clinical literature, released as open-source code and an open-access dataset. The SDV paper is cited only in a single general sentence supporting the claim that properly validated synthetic data can match real data in analytics and ML tasks without compromising privacy, with no SDV software used in the work.
paper-synthea-coronavirus-covid-model-20.needs: Affiliations not given in extracted text beyond superscript letters a/b/c with no institution names resolved.

paper-vine-copula-2019.summary: Casts vine copula structure selection as a reinforcement learning problem, learning tree structures that capture hierarchical dependence in tabular data better than greedy heuristics.

preprint-generative-federated-learning-i.summary: This is a survey paper reviewing generative AI (autoencoders, GANs, diffusion models, LLMs) and Federated Learning techniques applied to Intrusion Detection Systems, covering synthetic traffic generation, data augmentation, imputation, and adversarial traffic generation. It organizes prior IDS-related generative work and discusses open challenges in combining generative AI with federated IDS training. CTGAN and TVAE are cited as tabular data generation methods that provide 'the methodological basis for applying GANs to flow-based IDS datasets,' but neither is run or evaluated by the authors.

preprint-synthetic-financial-generation-.summary: This paper builds a unified multi-criteria evaluation framework for synthetic financial time series, comparing ARIMA-GARCH, VAEs, and TimeGAN on S&P 500 data across fidelity (MMD), temporal structure, and downstream utility (portfolio optimization, volatility forecasting), finding TimeGAN offers the best realism-coherence trade-off. SDV and CTGAN are cited only in passing, in a list of works illustrating that privacy regulations and acquisition costs constrain access to financial data.

preprint-fairtabgen-high-fidelity-fair-2.summary: Proposes FairTabGen, an LLM-based tabular data generation framework that uses in-context learning, curated prompts, and embedded structural constraints to synthesize fair, high-utility synthetic healthcare data from only a small subset of the original dataset, evaluated on MIMIC-IV. The paper positions its approach against prior generative methods, noting that CTGAN, TabDDPM, and REaLTabFormer emphasize statistical fidelity but often fail to address fairness when structural biases are encoded in training data. CTGAN is cited only as related-work prior art the authors depart from, not run in any experiment.
preprint-fairtabgen-high-fidelity-fair-2.needs: None; no SDV-family code or concept is run, only cited as comparison prior art.

preprint-mia-ept-membership-inference-20.summary: This paper introduces MIA-EPT, a black-box membership inference attack against tabular diffusion-model synthesizers that constructs error-based feature vectors by masking and reconstructing record attributes to reveal membership signals. It validates the attack on three diffusion-based synthesizers and reports results under the MIDST 2025 competition, showing substantial membership leakage in synthetic tabular data. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of GAN-based tabular generation contrasted with diffusion models, with no experiment run.

preprint-privacy-preserving-fair-synthet.summary: This paper proposes PF-WGAN, a privacy-preserving and fairness-constrained synthetic tabular data generator built by modifying the WGAN-GP architecture, and evaluates it against three state-of-the-art synthetic data generators across four datasets on utility, privacy, and fairness trade-offs. In its related-work discussion of GAN-based tabular synthesis methods, the paper lists TGAN, CTGAN, and CopulaGAN as popular prior approaches. CTGAN and TGAN (and the SDV-shipped CopulaGAN) are only named and cited as prior art in this discussion, with no evidence they were run as experimental baselines.
preprint-privacy-preserving-fair-synthet.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether the three comparison baselines mentioned in the abstract include CTGAN/CopulaGAN or entirely different models -- only the related-work listing is confirmed.

preprint-probabilistic-hash-embeddings-o.summary: This paper studies online learning of embeddings for categorical features whose vocabulary grows unboundedly over a data stream, proposing a probabilistic hash embedding (PHE) model with Bayesian online inference that avoids catastrophic forgetting and is invariant to item arrival order. It validates the approach on classification, sequence modeling, and recommendation tasks with high memory efficiency relative to one-hot embedding tables. CTGAN is mentioned only in a single related-work sentence describing it as a VAE/GAN-based tabular data generator that conditions on discrete categorical features, with no experiments run using it.

paper-tabgen-icl-2025.summary: Generates tabular data by prompting a fixed large language model rather than fine-tuning one, selecting in-context examples that cover the residual between the real distribution and what has been generated so far, so each round of prompting corrects the gap the previous round left. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN-based and VAE-based entries among the deep generative baselines it is measured against on marginal, correlation, precision, recall, C2ST and Jensen-Shannon divergence.

preprint-ctsyn-foundation-model-cross-20.summary: This paper proposes CTSyn, a diffusion-based generative foundation model for tabular data that uses a cross-tabular autoencoder to unify heterogeneous tables into a shared latent space and a conditional latent diffusion transformer to generate samples conditioned on table schema, pre-trained across many datasets. It benchmarks CTSyn against a wide array of tabular synthesizers including SMOTE, TabDDPM, TabSyn, AIM, PATE-CTGAN and GReaT on statistical fidelity, utility, diversity and privacy metrics. CTGAN and TVAE (from the SDV-family CTGAN paper) are run as baseline generators using the official sdv-dev/CTGAN implementation with explicit constructor hyperparameters, one of several methods CTSyn is compared against.

paper-constrained-dgm-realistic-2024.summary: Points out that deep tabular generators routinely emit rows violating background knowledge that always holds in the real data, and proposes a differentiable constraint layer that is appended to any generator so that generated samples are projected onto the feasible region during training and sampling, evaluated over six tasks with hand-specified constraint sets. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five generators the layer is applied to, each becoming a named constrained variant, C-CTGAN and C-TVAE, whose constraint-violation rate and downstream utility are reported against the unmodified originals.
paper-constrained-dgm-realistic-2024.needs: confirm derivative_work at importance 4 for a model-agnostic layer that yields a named CTGAN variant among several, rather than the usual 5

preprint-tabular-synthesis-differential-.summary: A survey paper that comprehensively reviews differentially private tabular data synthesis methods, classifying them into statistical and deep-learning approaches across centralized and distributed settings, and comparing them on utility, privacy, and computational cost. It discusses CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and federated variants built on it (Fed-TGAN, DP-CTGAN), and separately notes Patki et al.'s use of Gaussian copulas for relational parent-child synthesis. SDV-family methods (CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and the SDV Gaussian copula relational approach) are discussed and described in prose as prior art, not run experimentally by the authors.

preprint-cuts-customizable-tabular-synth.summary: This paper introduces CuTS, a customizable tabular synthetic data generation framework that lets data owners specify statistical, logical, and fairness/privacy constraints via declarative expressions, using a differentiable loss derived from these specifications to fine-tune a pre-trained generator. It is evaluated against several state-of-the-art tabular synthesizers and privacy/fairness methods across four datasets, showing higher downstream utility at matched fairness or privacy levels. TVAE and CTGAN, described as prominent methods collected in the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), are run as comparison baselines that CuTS is benchmarked against.
preprint-cuts-customizable-tabular-synth.needs: Not fully clear whether TVAE/CTGAN were run via the sdv-dev/ctgan packages or reimplemented; no explicit library import or hyperparameter table confirming package use was found in the excerpted text.

preprint-tbart-transformer-autoregressiv.summary: This paper introduces DP-TBART, a transformer-based autoregressive model that generates differentially private synthetic tabular data, aiming to close the performance gap between deep-learning and marginal-based DP synthesis methods across ten datasets. The authors compare DP-TBART against marginal-based state-of-the-art (AIM) and several deep-learning baselines including DP-CTGAN, DP-MERF, DP-HFlow, and DP-NTK. CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) is cited only in passing as one of several prior GAN-based tabular synthesis approaches in related work. Their evaluation metrics -- including the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic and related quality scores reported in the main results table -- are explicitly adapted from the original Synthetic Data Vault paper (Patki et al., 2016), making SDV's quality-report style metrics part of the paper's core evaluation methodology without directly invoking the SDV library.
preprint-tbart-transformer-autoregressiv.needs: Unclear whether the SDV-derived evaluation metrics were computed via the actual sdmetrics/SDV codebase or reimplemented independently ('adapted from'); mechanism between citation_only and a metric-level port could not be verified from the excerpts.

preprint-augmentation-imbalanced-regress.summary: This paper addresses imbalanced continuous or discrete covariates in regression, proposing a two-step algorithm combining weighted resampling with data augmentation to explore a wider covariate support before re-weighting toward a target distribution. Six data-generation approaches are compared numerically, including copula, GAN, random forest, and interpolation methods, with an actuarial application illustrating the approach. Two of these six generators -- Gaussian Copula and a Conditional GAN -- are explicitly run 'using the python-package Synthetic Data Vault', making SDV's GaussianCopula and CTGAN synthesizers evaluation subjects alongside SynthPop, SMOTE, and mixture-model approaches.

preprint-augmentation-gan-increases-perf.summary: This conference paper trains a GAN to generate synthetic ECG signals from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database to augment an unbalanced dataset, using the synthetic data to train a classifier that is then tested on real ECG data, showing improved classification performance. CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) is mentioned only once in passing as an example of GAN-based tabular data synthesis, and does not appear anywhere else in the text; it is a bibliography-only citation, not something run in the study.

preprint-generating-imputing-tabular-dif.summary: This paper proposes Forest-Flow and Forest-VP, XGBoost-based score-diffusion and conditional-flow-matching methods for generating and imputing mixed-type tabular data, evaluated on a 27-dataset benchmark with 9 metrics against deep-learning generators and diffusion baselines. Among the comparison methods, GaussianCopula, TVAE, and CTGAN are explicitly run using the Synthetic Data Vault's implementations with default hyperparameters. SDV's GaussianCopula, TVAE, and CTGAN synthesizers are run as baselines among the several generative methods benchmarked against the authors' proposed approach.

preprint-irg-modular-synthetic-relationa.summary: This paper proposes IRG, a modular framework for synthesizing relational databases that handles complex relational schemas such as composite keys, multi-fold connected tables, and sequential intra-table correlations, which prior relational synthesizers cannot capture. IRG is evaluated against three prior-art baselines across ten real-world RDB datasets, showing better fidelity, utility, and constraint satisfaction. SDV, run via its official SDK (version 1.16.2) using the hierarchical modeling algorithm (HMA) and an independent relational modeling variant (IND), is used as a key comparison baseline, with the paper documenting where SDV-HMA fails outright due to memory blow-up on wide tables.

preprint-joint-distributional-learning-c.summary: This paper proposes a VAE-based generative model that uses a closed-form Cramer-Wold distance regularization and a two-step learning method to better align the aggregated posterior with the prior, aiming to improve joint distributional learning for high-dimensional tabular datasets with many categorical variables. The authors evaluate their approach's synthetic data generation performance against prior tabular synthesis methods discussed in related work. CTGAN is cited only in the related-work discussion, described as assuming continuous columns can be approximated via Gaussian mixture distributions to model the decoder, without being run in the experiments.

paper-tabddpm-2022.summary: Applies denoising diffusion to general tabular data by running Gaussian diffusion on the normalized continuous features and multinomial diffusion on the one-hot categorical features under a shared reverse model, and shows across a wide benchmark that the result beats the GAN and VAE alternatives on machine-learning efficiency and on marginal and correlation fidelity, with SMOTE the only competitive shallow method. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the compared generators, with TVAE described as the state-of-the-art tabular variational autoencoder and CTGAN as the best-known GAN-based synthesizer, and the paper's primary evaluation measure is the machine-learning efficiency protocol credited to Xu et al.

preprint-generative-adversarial-networks.summary: This paper compares tabular GAN methods (CTGAN and TableGAN) against traditional statistical disclosure-control synthesis methods (Synthpop, DataSynthesizer) for generating synthetic UK census microdata, evaluating both utility metrics and a disclosure-risk metric (Targeted Correct Attribution Probability). CTGAN is run as a Python package with default parameters as one of the four synthesis methods benchmarked, described as using 'mode-specific normalization' to handle non-Gaussian and multimodal distributions. CTGAN, from the SDV family, is executed and evaluated as one of several generators compared on utility and disclosure risk.

preprint-differentially-private-syntheti.summary: This paper surveys four differentially private generative-adversarial approaches to tabular data synthesis (DPGAN, PATE-GAN, DP-CTGAN, PATE-CTGAN), benchmarking them at scale on five public datasets and two internal industry ML scenarios, and proposes QUAIL, an ensemble method that pairs a DP synthesizer with a DP classifier to boost downstream utility. The authors take CTGAN's own architecture and modify its discriminator training with DP-SGD and the PATE framework to build the DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN variants that anchor most of the empirical results. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and conditional generator design are explicitly adopted and altered, making CTGAN's architecture the derivative substrate for two of the four synthesizers evaluated.

thesis-montanez-2018.summary: Lays out the software abstractions and architecture for building generative models over database systems, and introduces reversible data transforms (later the RDT library) as the mechanism that makes such modeling tractable.
